title: HeyGen vs D-ID: avatars, usage costs and commercial exports
summary: Compare HeyGen and D-ID for presenter videos: avatar setup, model credits, duration rounding, commercial rights, watermarks and separate live-avatar products.
body_markdown:
Choose HeyGen when its Studio editing, avatar options and export plan fit your finished presenter video. Choose D-ID when its photo or V4 presenter workflow, sentiment controls and account terms fit better. Both also have real-time avatar routes. For a commercial clip, check the exact model, usage charge, permission and watermark separately; a paid plan alone does not answer every delivery requirement.


Magic Hour publishes this comparison and offers competing media tools. We reviewed first-party workflows, credit guides and export terms on November 3, 2026. We did not run a matched avatar-quality, latency or conversion test. The twelve-clip budget is an illustrative calculation.

## Decide whether you need a video file or a conversation


A prerecorded presenter follows an approved script and produces a video you can review before publishing. A live avatar responds during an interaction. Those purchases involve different controls, operating costs and review work, even if the same provider offers both.


D-ID supports scripted video and real-time Avatar Agents. HeyGen also offers real-time interaction through LiveAvatar. HeyGen’s own FAQ says LiveAvatar has independent plans and settings, and its avatars are not cross-compatible with standard HeyGen avatars. Do not buy a video-creation plan assuming it funds a live deployment.


This comparison focuses on downloadable presenter videos. For either live route, separately evaluate conversation limits, knowledge, integrations, privacy and the supported human handoff. A good prerecorded export does not demonstrate a working support agent.


Sources:[D-ID product and agent scope](https://www.d-id.com/alternatives/d-id-vs-heygen/) ·[HeyGen LiveAvatar plan and avatar boundaries](https://help.heygen.com/en/articles/12758866-liveavatar-faq)


## Choose the avatar input and editing workflow


HeyGen distinguishes photo-based looks from video-based looks and different motion engines. Its avatar FAQ directs photo avatars toward Avatar IV, while a video-based Digital Twin can use a different engine. Choose the input you can legitimately supply, then inspect the selected model instead of treating every HeyGen avatar as the same product.


HeyGen also recommends previewing speech and individual scenes before final rendering. Changes to avatar scenes can consume credits when they are rendered again. For an onboarding clip, settle the pronunciation of the product name and the pace of the instructions before spending on the final version.


D-ID’s current V4 Studio workflow lets you select an Expressive avatar, choose a sentiment, select a voice and enter a script or upload audio. Backgrounds and media layers can be added before generation. A selectable stock presenter and a custom spokesperson are separate entitlements: D-ID’s V4 availability page identifies custom Enterprise avatars.


Shortlist HeyGen when its scene workflow and the available avatar input suit your production process. Shortlist D-ID when its available presenter and sentiment controls suit the message. Neither description proves a universal realism or lip-sync winner.


Sources:[HeyGen avatar models and preview workflow](https://help.heygen.com/en/articles/15544929-avatar-voice-faq-troubleshooting-best-practices-and-credits) ·[D-ID V4 Studio workflow](https://www.d-id.com/introducing-v4-expressive-avatars/) ·[D-ID V4 stock and custom availability](https://www.d-id.com/v4-expressive-visual-avatars-tech-specs/)


## Commercial permission and a clean export are different checks


D-ID’s published rights guide permits commercial use on Pro, Advanced and Enterprise, subject to rights in your inputs. Trial and Lite are personal-use plans. That makes an inexpensive evaluation tier a different purchase from a business publishing workflow.


Its watermark guide adds another distinction: Trial has a full-video watermark, Lite has D-ID branding, and Pro has a generic AI watermark. Advanced can use your own logo; Enterprise can replace or remove the watermark. Commercial permission on Pro therefore does not mean an entirely unmarked export.


HeyGen’s current Creator card lists removal of HeyGen branding and 1080p export. Its export help permits commercial distribution subject to input guidelines. Check permissions for the person, voice, script, music and source media; a provider’s license cannot authorize someone else’s likeness.


If your client requires a particular disclosure, logo treatment or delivery resolution, write it into the brief before choosing the tier. Review the final downloaded file, not only the editor preview.


Sources:[D-ID commercial-use rights by plan](https://help.d-id.com/hc/en-us/articles/31350883819537-What-are-the-copyright-and-commercial-use-rights-for-my-videos) ·[D-ID watermark rules by plan](https://help.d-id.com/hc/en-us/articles/31350550554641-How-do-I-change-or-remove-the-watermark-on-my-videos) ·[Current HeyGen plans](https://www.heygen.com/pricing) ·[HeyGen export and use guidance](https://help.heygen.com/en/articles/9834825-how-to-download-or-export-a-video)


## Compare the actual usage units


HeyGen’s newer plans use credits across supported generation features. Creator currently includes 600 monthly credits, but usage depends on the selected model and operation. Unlimited creation claims from an older plan should not be applied to a new subscription.


Its credit guide lists Avatar IV Photo Look at 16 credits per generated minute and Video Look at 31. Other operations, including custom motion and translation, have their own charges. The guide warns that account rates and limits can vary, so the quote shown before generation is authoritative for your account.


D-ID’s Studio FAQ says each generated video rounds up to the next fifteen-second interval. It also says unused minutes do not accumulate month to month. Check the selected plan’s current allowance and quote rather than copying an old comparison’s dollar price.


Use the amount you will actually purchase, including billing commitment and required export features. Neither a minute nor a credit is a standardized unit of avatar quality.


Sources:[HeyGen current credit model and rates](https://help.heygen.com/en/articles/15126059-how-to-use-credits-on-heygen) ·[D-ID Studio minute accounting](https://www.d-id.com/pricing/studio/)


## A worked brief: twelve short updates


Suppose you need twelve separate twenty-second presenter clips. That is four minutes of finished footage. Under D-ID’s published fifteen-second rounding rule, each clip consumes thirty seconds: six plan minutes before retries or translated versions.


For a hypothetical HeyGen Avatar IV Photo Look job where all 240 seconds require avatar generation, the standard 16-credit rate gives 64 credits. This assumes the stated rate applies and excludes additional operations. It is arithmetic, not an observed invoice or proof that the outputs have equivalent quality.


Add the cost of revisions you actually expect. Keep the approved script, selected voice and avatar, output duration, account quote and final file together. Budget language versions separately, then compare the subscription and review effort needed to produce the complete deliverable.


Sources:[D-ID duration rounding](https://www.d-id.com/pricing/studio/) ·[HeyGen standard avatar rates](https://help.heygen.com/en/articles/15126059-how-to-use-credits-on-heygen)


## Check the final handoff before moving a library


HeyGen’s export guide distinguishes an ordinary download from 4K and SCORM delivery. It reserves 4K downloads for specified higher plans and SCORM for Business and Enterprise. A plan that creates a suitable presenter is not automatically the plan your learning platform requires.


Use one representative script containing a product name, a number and a pause. Preview the voice, make one correction and inspect the exported captions, mouth movement, pacing, watermark and resolution. If localization is required, have a fluent reviewer check the actual translated message.


If your current workflow works, avoid an unnecessary move. HeyGen’s credit guide warns that cancelling or switching a legacy plan can prevent a return. Retain your scripts and permitted source files.


If the narrower task is animating one portrait with an existing voice track, Magic Hour Talking Photo is another route to evaluate. It starts from a portrait and supplied audio; it is not a claim to replace every scene editor or live-agent feature.
